sources.title: Few-shot adaptation of multi-modal foundation models: a survey
sources.snippet: To effectively enhance the model's generalization performance in specific domains, it is necessary to fine-tune multi-modal foundation models using limited samples, enabling them to have broader applications. These methods can be defined as few-shot adaptation methods for multi-modal foundation models.

sources.title: Few-Shot Multimodal Medical Imaging: A Theoretical Framework
sources.snippet: The process begins by feeding both abundant and limited labeled datasets into a learning frame-work that integrates few-shot samples within a theoretical model fθ. The model is built to not only deliver diagnostic predictions, but also report how confident those predictions are and explain the reasoning behind them.

sources.title: Few-shot Adaptation of Multi-modal Foundation Models: A Survey
sources.snippet: Multi-modal (vision-language) models, such as CLIP, are replacing traditional supervised pre-training models (e.g., ImageNet-based pre-training) as the new generation of visual foundation models. These models with robust and aligned semantic representations learned from billions of internet image-text pairs and can be applied to various downstream tasks in a zero-shot manner. sources.title: Multimodal Large Models in Few-Shot Learning Scenarios
sources.snippet: Multimodal large models (MLLMs) have recently demonstrated significant potential in addressing the challenge of few-shot learning across various tasks. By integrating information from different modalities such as vision, language, and audio, these models offer enhanced generalization and contextual understanding, which are essential when training data is limited.
